1.explanation: ReplaceOptions.js defines the two replace actions for parallel vs. sequential multi-instance subprocesses and specifies new loopCharacteristics on the target businessObject. BpmnReplace.js is responsible for applying these target.options when performing the replace. Its copyProperties/pick logic only copies a hard-coded list of CUSTOM_PROPERTIES (which excludes loopCharacteristics) and thus never applies the loopCharacteristics defined in ReplaceOptions.js. As a result, when toggling the MI type, the existing cardinality (loopCharacteristics) is dropped.
1.bug_scenario: The GIF shows a user modeling a collapsed subprocess and configuring it as a multi-instance subprocess. First they select the subprocess and switch it to parallel multi-instance, then enter a loop cardinality of 4. Next they toggle the multi-instance type from parallel to sequential in the properties panel. Immediately upon switching, the previously entered loop cardinality disappears (and other MI settings are lost) – the subprocess retains the multi-instance marker in the diagram, but its cardinality field resets.
